claims.text: Sustained high-temperature loading causes progressive plastic deformation or creep in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers through dislocation nucleation and motion.
Dislocation nucleation during creep is mediated by the FCC/BCC interfaces.
Local chemical short-range order modulates dislocation mobility.
Lattice distortion and chemically driven short-range order at nanoscale interfaces dynamically alter the activation barrier for dislocation motion.
Evolution of short-range order produces a transition from initially suppressed plasticity to gradually accelerated creep.
The starting coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers with severe lattice distortion and some chemical short-range order.
Applied stress and temperature influence creep behavior in high-entropy materials.
Changing bilayer thickness or applying a pre-anneal can alter the degree of short-range order.
The nanoscale FCC/BCC interfaces and local short-range-ordered domains control dislocation nucleation and motion.
Sustained loading creates localized stress accumulation at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Short-range order initially increases the barrier to dislocation nucleation.
Prolonged exposure to high temperature rearranges short-range order and interface structure, thereby reducing dislocation barriers.
Reduced barriers permit interfacial dislocation arrays to nucleate and cross the interfaces, progressively facilitating creep.
Dislocations initially confined by interfaces will nucleate more readily as local short-range order evolves.
Sustained loading will increase interfacial dislocation density.
A specimen with evolving or enhanced short-range order will exhibit a higher creep strain rate than a chemically more random baseline specimen.
An as-deposited multilayer with minimal induced short-range order and less-developed interfacial dislocation structures has a lower creep rate under otherwise identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism is limited to conditions that retain the nanoscale multilayer architecture and avoid catastrophic phase transformation or layer degradation.
The relative contributions of interfaces and bulk layers to creep may vary with composition and bilayer thickness.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that short-range order initially raises the dislocation-nucleation barrier, while the prediction and falsification rule expect enhanced short-range order to produce accelerated nucleation and higher creep. A possible time-dependent reversal is proposed, but the comparison and falsification rule do not specify the duration or crossover point needed to distinguish initial suppression from later acceleration.
